translationRepairs: Li Jianji was from Xu Prefecture.
s0001 reads 許州人; 許州 is Xu Prefecture (Xuchang region), not 徐州. Rendering it as Xuzhou invents the wrong place, and Xu Prefecture restores the source.
Li Jianji was a native of Xuzhou.
Li Jianji was a native of Xu Prefecture.
The literal likewise turns 許州 into Xuzhou; Xu Prefecture matches the Chinese place-name and avoids confusion with 徐州.
The court posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Preceptor.
The court posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Commandant.
詔贈太尉 records a posthumous grant of 太尉 (Grand Commandant), not 太師 (Grand Preceptor); the proposed title is the correct office.
An edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Preceptor.
An edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Commandant.
The literal also mistranslates 太尉 as Grand Preceptor; Grand Commandant is the accurate English for that title.
His father Jingrou had been prefect in turn of Ying, Ping, Ru, Tan, and Ying.
His father Jingrou had been prefect in turn of Ying, Ping, Ru, Tan, and a second Ying Prefecture.

The source lists five prefectures 瀛、平、儒、檀、營; the first and last are distinct places both romanized Ying. Calling the latter a second Ying Prefecture preserves the distinction without inserting Chinese characters into the English text.
